plants.name: Camellia japonica
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy dark green leaves and rose-like flowers. It thrives in cool, humid conditions and is widely cultivated in gardens in warm temperate regions, where it brightens the dead of winter.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (December to March in the Northern Hemisphere)
plants.location: Native to Japan, Korea and China; cultivated in the southeastern United States, Europe, and Australia
plants.funFact: Camellia japonica is a close relative of the tea plant (Camellia sinensis), and its seeds are pressed to produce camellia oil used in cooking and cosmetics.

plants.name: Hamamelis mollis
plants.description: A deciduous large shrub or small tree that produces spidery, ribbon-like, fragrant flowers on bare branches in mid-winter. The blooms tolerate frost by curling up in freezing temperatures and unfurling again when it warms.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid to late winter (January to March)
plants.location: Native to central and eastern China; grown in temperate gardens across Europe and North America
plants.funFact: Witch hazel flowers curl their petals into tight spirals during cold snaps to protect themselves, then relax once temperatures rise.

plants.name: Delonix regia
plants.description: A spreading tree with fern-like leaves that becomes a spectacular canopy of fiery blossoms. In the Southern Hemisphere summer, it blooms in tropical and subtropical regions, with streets and parks glowing red-orange.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer in the Southern Hemisphere (December to February); dry season in some tropical regions
plants.location: Native to Madagascar; widely planted in northern Australia, Brazil, southern Africa, and tropical Asia
plants.funFact: Although it is one of the most celebrated tropical ornamental trees, the flamboyant is endangered in its native Madagascar.

plants.name: Protea cynaroides
plants.description: A shrub with the largest flower head in the Protea genus, resembling a giant artichoke with a crown of silky pink bracts. It grows in fynbos habitat and flowers heavily in the Southern Hemisphere's summer, attracting sunbirds and beetles.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to summer in the Southern Hemisphere, with peak bloom from about November to February in cultivation
plants.location: Native to the Cape region of South Africa; cultivated in Australia, California, Hawaii, and New Zealand
plants.funFact: The king protea is the national flower of South Africa, and its genus is named after Proteus, the Greek sea god who could change his shape.
